one_liner: Assemble and parameter-count a from-scratch 100M-parameter transformer from named, cited 2024-2026 SOTA components.

key_terms.definition: Trading network width (d_model) for depth (n_layers) at a fixed parameter budget; sub-billion models favor many narrow layers over few wide ones (MobileLLM, 2024).
Attention variant where multiple query heads share fewer key-value heads, shrinking the KV cache (here 4x) with minimal quality loss versus full multi-head attention.
RMSNorm applied to query and key vectors per head before the dot product, bounding attention-logit magnitude by construction and preventing softmax-saturation blowups at high learning rates.
A normalization layer that scales activations by the inverse root-mean-square (no mean-subtraction or bias), cheaper than LayerNorm and computed in fp32 for stability.
Positional encoding that rotates 2D slices of query/key vectors by an angle proportional to position, making attention scores depend only on relative offset.
Omitting explicit positional encoding on certain layers, relying on the causal mask alone to convey position; interleaved every 4th layer here to aid length generalization.
A gated MLP variant using three weight matrices (gate, up, down) with a SiLU-activated gate multiplying a linear path, replacing the vanilla two-matrix FFN.
An auxiliary training penalty on the squared log-sum-exp of the output logits that keeps the softmax's log-partition function near zero, improving numerical conditioning.
A Gemma-2-style tanh squashing of logits, z <- c*tanh(z/c), that hard-bounds them to (-c, c); used optionally on attention or final logits for extra stability.
Sharing a single weight matrix between the input token embedding and the output (lm_head) projection, saving parameters and improving small-model quality (Press & Wolf, 2017).
DeepSeek-V2's attention variant that compresses K/V into a small cached latent vector, up-projecting to per-head K/V on the fly, with a decoupled RoPE key to preserve positional compatibility.
An auxiliary training head (DeepSeek-V3) that predicts a token further ahead (e.g. t+2) alongside the main next-token objective, densifying the training signal and enabling self-speculative decoding.
